item.title: Still got wings: The Briefing for 16 February 2026
item.description: Red Bull has not exhausted its energy for challenging EU dawn raids on its premises, asking the European Court of Justice to set aside a lower court ruling that upheld an inspection decision last year. The company claims the EU General Court committed errors of law and procedure in appeal grounds published today. Also in The Briefing, Greece’s antitrust enforcer inches closer to an abuse of domina...

item.title: Senate democrats urge CFIUS probe into UAE–backed crypto acquisition
item.description: A United Arab Emirates-backed fund’s reported $500 million acquisition of a stake in the Trump family’s cryptocurrency business raises “significant” national security concerns over access to sensitive data, two democratic party senators have told the US Treasury Secretary.

item.title: EU closes abuse probe into Edwards Lifesciences
item.description: Edwards Lifesciences has escaped an EU abuse of dominance probe by removing an "anti-copycatting" policy after the European Commission raised concerns that it could foreclose a rival.

item.title: Market tools: The Briefing for 17 February 2026
item.description: Sweden’s Competition Authority could join the ranks of agencies with new market investigation tools this summer, although unlike its counterparts, the proposed powers would not allow the enforcer to impose asset divestments. The government announced the proposal last week, which must be approved by the country’s parliament. Also in The Briefing, the Swiss enforcer lifts the lid on the targets of a...

item.title: UK consumer group to withdraw Qualcomm collective action
item.description: A UK consumer rights organisation has agreed to withdraw its £480 million class action lawsuit against Qualcomm following a five-week trial, conceding its antitrust arguments before the Competition Appeal Tribunal would have failed.

item.title: Lear opens first office outside of Italy
item.description: Italian economic consultancy Lear has hired the former chief economist at Portugal's Competition Authority to co-head its newly established Lisbon office.

item.title: Assefi asks staff to “empty the clip”
item.description: The Department of Justice’s antitrust division has been far too timid in bringing civil enforcement actions, the acting head of the agency has said, challenging staff to “keep up with the pace we have set in the criminal programme”.

item.title: Hard reset: The Tipline for 17 February 2026
item.description: Paramount is hoping this reboot fares better than Frasier 2.0. Warner Bros Discovery has given Paramount one week to improve its offer ahead of a 20 March shareholder meeting to seek approval for Netflix’s offer. Warner Bros chief executive David Zaslav said he had given Paramount “clear direction on the deficiencies in their offers and opportunities to address them”. Also in Tipline, Makan Delrah...

item.title: States accuse DOJ of withholding “substantial” HPE docs
item.description: The Colorado-led state challengers to the Hewlett Packard Enterprises/Juniper Networks approval have claimed the Department of Justice is stonewalling their bid to obtain crucial evidence about the controversial settlement.
